links.comparator_used: Same model given the same data and prompted to summarize it with no rules (unconstrained LLM baseline)
links.outcome: Accuracy of numerical and categorical statements in generated clinical summaries
links.effect: 1 substantive content error across 2,067 harness checks (0.05%) for the constrained pipeline vs about two in five checkable numerical statements wrong in the unconstrained baseline; no hard errors in the narrative prose
links.tradeoff: Soft errors (information combined across waves or measures) in 8 of 25 briefs (32%), which the harness does not check; clinician review incomplete (4 of 7 target)
links.quote: Across the three models (Gemma 4 31B, Gemini 3 Flash, GPT-4.1), the harness identified one substantive content error, meaning one that would change a clinician’s reading, for a rate of 0.05%, against an unconstrained baseline in which about two in five checkable numerical statements were wrong.

links.comparator_used: Unconstrained baseline summaries from the same model without the rules and evidence-ID design
links.outcome: Traceability of statements to source data
links.effect: Every constrained brief carried a traceable evidence-ID on each statement; every unconstrained baseline brief contained at least one statement with no traceable basis in the source data
links.quote: Every constrained brief also carried a traceable evidence-ID on each statement, as the design requires, while every unconstrained baseline brief contained at least one statement with no traceable basis in the source data.

design_hint: rules-based data constraint and evidence-ID grounding pipeline
